title: Slow English Podcast #141: Republic of Kongo

sentences.text: Today, we will talk about the Republic of the Congo.
It is a green, tropical and peaceful country in Central Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is the Republic of the Congo?
The Republic of the Congo is in Central Africa.
It is next to Gabon, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Angola, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
It also has a short coast on the Atlantic Ocean.
It is different from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
They are two separate countries.
What is the capital city of the Republic of the Congo?
The capital city is Brazzaville.
Brazzaville is next to the Congo River, right across from Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Other cities include Pointe Noir near the ocean, Dolize and Owando.
How many people live in the Republic of the Congo?
About 6 million people live in the country.
Most people live in Brazzaville, Pointe Noir, or along the Congo River.
There are many ethnic groups and languages, and people are known for being friendly and welcoming.
What language do people speak in the Republic of the Congo?
The official language is French.
People also speak many local languages, such as Lingala Kituba, also called Munukutuba, Teke and Bochi.
Many people speak more than one language in daily life.
What is the weather like in the Republic of the Congo?
The country has a tropical climate.
That means it is hot and humid most of the year.
There is a rainy season and a dry season.
It rains a lot in the north and in the forest areas.
What does the Republic of the Congo look like?
The country has thick rainforests, rivers and swamps, mountains and hills in the south, beaches on the Atlantic coast, the large Congo River, one of Africa's biggest rivers.
Nature is wild and full of green trees and animals.
What animals live in the Republic of the Congo?
In the forests and rivers, you can find gorillas and chimpanzees, elephants, antelopes and buffalo, crocodiles and hippos, parrots, monkeys and eagles, many types of fish, frogs and insects.
Some parks protect endangered animals, especially gorillas.
What do people eat in the Republic of the Congo?
Food in Congo is local, fresh and often spicy.

People eat, cassava boiled or made into fufu, plantains and yams, fish, chicken or goat meat, peanut sauce, leafy greens and rice, popular dishes, saka -saka, pounded cassava leaves, moambe chicken, chicken and palm butter sauce, fufu, a soft dough eaten with soup or sauce, grilled fish with chili and lemon.
People eat with hands or with spoons depending on the meal.
What do people drink in the Republic of the Congo?
People drink water palm wine, a sweet drink from palm trees, fruit juices, mango, pineapple, guava, herbal teas and coffee.
In rural areas, people may also drink fermented drinks made from corn or cassava.
What is life like in the Republic of the Congo?
Life is often simple and community based.
People enjoy talking with neighbors, going to markets, attending church, playing drums and dancing, watching football soccer, the most popular sport.
Many people work in farming, fishing or local trade.
What are some holidays and traditions in the Republic of the Congo?
Independence Day, August 15th, Labor Day, May 1st, Christmas and Easter, New Year's Day, local festivals with music, dancing and traditional dress.
At celebrations, people dance to drums, sing in groups and eat together as a community.
Some fun facts about the Republic of the Congo.
The flag is green, yellow and red.
The Congo River is the deepest river in the world.
Brazzaville and Kinshasa are the closest capital cities in the world.
The country has one of the largest rainforests in Africa.
Music and dance are a big part of daily life.
Now you know many things about the Republic of the Congo.
You know where it is, what people speak and what they eat.
You learned about nature, culture and daily life.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emile.
See you next time.
Goodbye.
Or, as they say in French, au revoir.
